transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-23 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 min | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Ellen (CFO, Nimbus), Samir (Legal), Priya (Head of Security), Jason (Platform), Meera (PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:04] Ellen Park: Yeah, can hear you. Thanks for fitting this in, we wanted to run through the commercial clearance items before procurement kicks it to pricing committee.
[00:11] Lucas Rivera: Great, I can cover the tech feasibility side, especially migration paths and what a dedicated capacity pilot looks like.
[00:18] Samir Patel: From legal, real quick, we'll want an MSA excerpt that shows liability caps, data handling, and the DPA summary. Also curious about indemnities for model outputs.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Totally — we'll provide a redline-friendly MSA snippet. And we'll surface the standard DPA; there's a short version we can share that lists EU data residency options.
[00:36] Dr. Priya Nair: On security, our primary asks are: SSO/SAML integration, KMS for customer-managed keys, and audit logs retention. Also SOC2 Type II evidence.
[00:46] Maya Chen: That's expected. Redwood supports SAML SSO, customer KMS via cloud-provider integrations or HSM through our Private offering, and we can produce audit logs. We also have SOC2 Type II reports — I'll share the latest.
[00:56] Jason Kline: Quick Q on private deployment: can you run in our VPC and keep KV caches local? We can't have cross-tenant caches for compliance.
[01:05] Lucas Rivera: Yes, Private offers a VPC-deployed plane, KV cache stays within customer boundary. There's an on-prem connector if you need air-gapped. Note, that path affects latency and cost a bit.
[01:18] Ellen Park: Cost bit — that's the thing. Procurement wants a hard egress and per-month estimate for a 12-month commit at our projected 10M tokens/month. We need scenarios for hosted vs dedicated.
[01:30] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prepare a pricing sheet showing three tiers: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit with burst), and private on-prem pricing. We'll break out egress fees and token unit economics.
[01:41] Meera Joshi: Also timeline: Legal wants to know if a pilot can start before MSA sign-off or do you require full contract?
[01:49] Maya Chen: Normally we can do a short-term eval via our hosted API under standard terms, but for reserved/dedicated capacity and Private we need a commercial agreement and DPA. For a pilot with reserved capacity we typically do a Letter of Intent or short pilot addendum.
[02:03] Samir Patel: That may work. We'll aim to propose a limited-scope pilot addendum. We still need clarity on SLA numbers — what's Redwood's SLA for Dedicated?
[02:12] Lucas Rivera: For Dedicated, typical SLA is 99.9% for request success and p99 latency targets depend on model/profile — we can commit to latency bands for your workloads after benchmarks. For Hosted, SLA is standard, but Dedicated has stronger uptime guarantees and rollback/fallback to other model variants if overloaded.
[02:28] Ellen Park: 99.9 vs procurement's ask of 99.95 — is that a negotiable point?
[02:33] Maya Chen: We can discuss escalation tiers and financial credits. 99.95 on Dedicated is possible with specific capacity and ops commitments — it's usually part of an enterprise SLA addendum and depends on reserve levels.
[02:44] Dr. Priya Nair: On encryption: are keys customer-controlled in Private? We need KMS where keys never leave our control. Also zero-knowledge on model telemetry.
[02:54] Lucas Rivera: Yes, Private supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or HSM; telemetry can be minimized and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll capture exact requirements in the security deep dive.
[03:06] Speaker 1: (inaudible) you mentioned telemetry — can logs be filtered to exclude content?
[03:11] Lucas Rivera: We can mask PII and only log metadata, but we'll need to align on what counts as PII in your policy.
[03:19] Meera Joshi: For procurement: egress — we have to present worst-case and expected-case egress charges to finance. Can you give examples?
[03:27] Maya Chen: We'll produce an egress worksheet. For instance, a 10M token/month workload with a 1:3 request-to-response token ratio will have X GB egress; we will show the math and the estimated per-GB fees. We'll provide low/med/high scenario columns.
[03:41] Jason Kline: Migration feasibility — if we start with hosted, what's the path to move to Dedicated without major API changes?
[03:48] Lucas Rivera: API compatibility is maintained. We have version pinning and model aliasing. Moving to Dedicated is mostly a config/route change and data plane provisioning; you can keep the same integration with minimal code changes. There are caveats around caching behavior and sequence length defaults — we'll document best practices.
[04:05] Ellen Park: Procurement wants to know about termination rights and data deletion on contract end. What's your standard?
[04:12] Maya Chen: Standard is data deletion within 30 days post-termination, with audit log of deletion. For Private/on-prem we provide tooling to remove local artifacts; for Hosted we purge customer data per the DPA. We'll include specific clauses.
[04:25] Samir Patel: On indemnities for generated content — that's a sticky area. How do you handle model hallucination risks?
[04:32] Lucas Rivera: We have safety disclaimers and can provide model configuration options to be more conservative. Legal-ish answer: indemnity scope can be negotiated; typical approach is carve-outs for misuse and dependent on product. We'll flag this for legal redline.
[04:48] Maya Chen: We should also surface the Optimize tooling — batching and caching profiles reduce cost. For a 10M token workload, Optimize can materially cut cost; Lucas can include estimated savings in the benchmark.
[04:59] Lucas Rivera: I will run three bench runs: baseline hosted latency, dedicated with default batching, and dedicated with optimized KV caching, and show per-token and per-hour GPU costs.
[05:10] Dr. Priya Nair: Also request: we need to validate KMS key lifecycle and rotation policy. Is there an API to rotate keys without downtime?
[05:18] Lucas Rivera: Yes, rotation is supported. We can stage keys and rotate with zero-downtime if configured. We'll demo during the security dive.
[05:28] Ellen Park: On pricing committee dynamics — I lead finance but we have a procurement gate that usually requires three quotes. Any standard rebuttal to that?
[05:36] Maya Chen: We often provide detailed TCO models that show total cost of ownership against alternatives, and references. Also a pilot commitment can reduce the procurement friction.
[05:45] Meera Joshi: Timelines — if we get pricing by Friday (2025-06-27) and security doc by next week, procurement can try to include this in their July 12 pricing committee. Does that align?
[05:56] Maya Chen: Yes, that's plausible.
[05:59] Samir Patel: A few redline items I'll flag now: liabilities cap at 2x fees looks low for us; we may ask for higher; also audit rights for the DPA — we need to negotiate scope.
[06:11] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll surface typical counter-proposals we see and your legal can pick language.
[06:16] Jason Kline: A practical question: how do you handle IP firewalling? Can requests be restricted to allowlisted IPs?
[06:23] Lucas Rivera: Yes, IP allowlisting and VPC endpoints supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted has API key controls and network restrictions depending on plan.
[06:35] Speaker 1: (overlap) latency numbers — do you have p50/p95/p99 for comparable customers?
[06:40] Lucas Rivera: We can share anonymized profiles. For 8k context Llama-2 style models on Dedicated, p50 is typically 20-60ms per token for streaming; p99 depends on batching and peak concurrency. Bench will make this concrete.
[06:54] Ellen Park: Ok, let's summarize next steps.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya to send pricing worksheet + MSA excerpt + SOC2 and DPA summary by 2025-06-27. Lucas will run perf/cost bench and share spreadsheet by 2025-06-30. Security deep dive scheduled tentatively for 2025-07-02 — we'll send calendar invite. Samir to share legal redlines by 2025-07-03.
[07:20] Samir Patel: Sounds good.
[07:22] Dr. Priya Nair: One more ask — can Redwood confirm data residency pathways for EU customers in writing? We need explicit host region names.
[07:30] Maya Chen: We'll include the EU region hostnames and the Private deployment options in the security packet.
[07:37] Ellen Park: Thanks, team. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[07:41] Maya Chen: None. We'll get to work and follow-up.
[07:44] Speaker 1: (inaudible) thanks all.
